Stage 1 — what this repo ALREADY does, in four states rather than two.

The two-state version (has it / doesn't) is what makes an agent go port something that is already in the tree. Recorded instances from the source project: iterative refinement was present but every inter-layer reference was `.clone().detach()`, so it was look-forward-ONCE and DINO's look-forward-twice was the thing actually missing; one-to-many positives were present but on the main branch instead of the aux branch, which was the fault itself. A two-state audit writes both as ❌ and sends you to port what you have.
_comment_states:
present            ✅ complete implementation   — cite function name + call site
present_defeated   ⚠️ implemented, and one line voids it — ‼️ NAME THAT LINE
absent             ❌ genuinely not there       — grepped at least two namings
absent_deliberate  🅾️ absent, and it was a trade — say what the budget bought instead

🅾️ carries weight the others do not: a 3D paper skipping deformable attention may have spent that budget on its own contribution. Ask why the author would skip it BEFORE deciding to copy it back.
_comment_entries:
One per technique examined: {technique, state, evidence, defeated_at, traded_for, checked_namings[]}

`evidence` is a file:line a reader can open — not a recollection. `defeated_at` is required when state is `present_defeated` and is the entire value of that state. `checked_namings` is required when state is `absent`, because "I grepped for it" and "I grepped for the one name I happened to think of" are different claims.
_comment_cost_profile:
Stage 1.5 — the cost profile taken in the same pass, because a hyperparameter forced by cost can be the root of an accuracy bug. The recorded chain: an RPE cost of `nqueries × preenc_npoints` pinned `nqueries` from 1024 to 256, so 47% of production frames filled every query with a positive, the classifier never saw a negative, objectness saturated at 0.999, and NMS greedy ordering became a coin flip.

The signature to recognize: 100% reported utilization at 154 W of 700 W, TF32 ineffective (0.93x), throughput flat from batch 8 to 48 — all serialized on one kernel.
